hook: Dario Amodei trained as a physicist, earning a Ph.D. in biophysics from Princeton as a Hertz Fellow before moving into machine learning at Baidu, briefly at Google Brain, and then at OpenAI. As OpenAI's Vice President of Research, he set research direction, led the teams that built GPT-2 and GPT-3, and helped pioneer reinforcement learning from human feedback. In 2021 he left to co-found Anthropic, where as CEO he has pushed the idea that AI safety and frontier capability can be built together rather than traded off. He argues that case publicly too, from his 2024 essay Machines of Loving Grace on AI's potential upside to a 2025 New York Times op-ed calling for basic transparency rules on frontier AI development.
name: Dario Amodei

quote.text: I think that most people are underestimating just how radical the upside of AI could be.
quote.context: From Dario Amodei's essay Machines of Loving Grace, darioamodei.com, October 2024

primary.name: Dario Amodei, Machines of Loving Grace

secondary.name: Alex Kantrowitz, The Making of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

timeline.event: Completes a Ph.D. in biophysics at Princeton University as a Hertz Fellow, then does postdoctoral research in computational neuroscience at Stanford University School of Medicine
timeline.impact: Builds a research base in measuring neural circuit behavior before moving into machine learning

timeline.event: Joins Baidu's AI team, recruited by Andrew Ng
timeline.impact: Moves from academic neuroscience into industrial deep learning research
Continues deep learning research before joining OpenAI

timeline.event: Joins OpenAI, rising to Vice President of Research
timeline.impact: Sets research direction, leads GPT-2 development, and helps pioneer reinforcement learning from human feedback

timeline.event: Leads the GPT-3 project and departs OpenAI in December
timeline.impact: GPT-3 becomes one of the largest language models trained to date, and his departure precedes founding Anthropic
Starts a public benefit corporation focused on building safe, interpretable AI systems, later producing the Claude model family

timeline.event: Publishes the essay Machines of Loving Grace in October
timeline.impact: Argues AI's potential upside for medicine, neuroscience and economic development is widely underestimated

timeline.event: Writes a New York Times op-ed calling for basic AI transparency rules
timeline.impact: Pushes the public policy debate toward mandatory disclosure requirements for frontier AI developers

quick_facts: Co-founder and CEO of Anthropic, a public benefit corporation focused on AI safety
Previously Vice President of Research at OpenAI, where he led development of GPT-2 and GPT-3 and helped originate reinforcement learning from human feedback
Holds a Ph.D. in biophysics from Princeton University as a Hertz Fellow, and did postdoctoral research in computational neuroscience at Stanford University School of Medicine
Co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with his sister Daniela Amodei and several OpenAI colleagues
Author of the essay Machines of Loving Grace (October 2024) and a 2025 New York Times op-ed on AI transparency rules

achievements.title: Vice President of Research, OpenAI
achievements.impact: Set research direction and led the teams that built GPT-2 and GPT-3, and helped originate reinforcement learning from human feedback as a training technique.

achievements.title: Co-founder and CEO, Anthropic
achievements.impact: Built an AI safety-focused lab and the Claude model family around the goal of making AI systems reliable, interpretable and steerable.

achievements.title: Machines of Loving Grace essay, 2024
achievements.impact: Set out a detailed, widely discussed case for how advanced AI could accelerate progress in medicine, neuroscience and economic development.

achievements.title: Public advocacy for AI transparency
achievements.impact: Argued in a 2025 New York Times op-ed for basic transparency rules governing frontier AI development.
